validation.count_scope: Harness checks count one native program execution or one compiler/CLI rejection; CPython reference executions and successful compilation subprocesses are additional and are not included in these totals.

limits: Generated LLVM and runtime sources are instrumented; the prebuilt Rust standard library is not rebuilt with ASan.

cache_and_process_scope.cache_kind: Twelve existing timestamp-based CPython 3.14 caches have valid headers and unchanged source/cache hashes before and after both runs.
cache_and_process_scope.fresh_process: Each measured engine run starts a fresh subprocess; filesystem fixture cwd is fresh per inventory run.
cache_and_process_scope.not_isolated: CPU affinity is [0], but the shared devbox is not dedicated or kernel-isolated. No cache flush, cold-page-cache guarantee, fsync, fixed hash seed, or identical allocator/representation is claimed.
cache_and_process_scope.timing: Whole subprocess wall time includes startup/imports, parsing, eager collections, fulfillment, complete report I/O, flush/close, and exit. Fixture setup, oracle checks, full-output verification/hashing, compilation, warmups, and cleanup are outside retained samples.
cache_and_process_scope.order: Thirty retained rounds use all six permutations five times. Within-round positions and directed adjacent pairs balance; cross-round predecessors and the two warmups do not balance.

contract_and_fairness: Zero-based original batch/row positions; positive requests only; duplicate stock last value wins while first insertion controls report order; requested order comes from a dict, never set traversal.
Unknown SKUs have zero availability and never create remaining-stock rows. The requested set selects the untouched-stock section.
Both inputs are read and closed before report open. Stock parse precedes opening orders. Output may truncate or partially write; it is not atomic.
Malformed input and device output failures are validated but are not timed workloads. The boundary workload exercises successful arbitrary-precision quantities.

All three inventory engines implement the same eager algorithm and arbitrary-precision quantities. Rust uses borrowed SKU/request references, native collections, and direct formatting, so allocation and ownership representation differ.
Supported common input domain uses ASCII decimal digits with permitted signs/underscores, valid UTF-8 argv, and the documented normalized errors. CPython tracebacks/context/chaining are not matched.

Ordinary and matched ThinLTO comparisons are separate; Rust LLVM 22.1.8 differs from Clang 18.1.3 generating Relar IR. ThinLTO uses Rust LLD 22.1.8 and explicit 1000 import/inline budgets on both native implementations.
The old-source control has byte-identical emitted IR and runtime archive bytes, but executable hashes differ. Small timing differences do not establish a comprehension overhead regression or gain.
